bottom_line: GIFT Nifty signals a gap-up start for Indian equities following Monday's sharp sell-off, despite severe tech-led declines across Asian markets this morning.
Global technology stocks faced renewed selling pressure as Nvidia's Monday rally unwound, sending South Korea's Kospi down 5.30% and Taiwan's TAIEX down 7.21%.
Commodities saw broad profit-booking, with gold dropping 2.43% to $3,562.70 and silver sinking 4.65%, providing cost relief to domestic manufacturing sectors.

global.us: Wall Street closed mixed on Tuesday as early enthusiasm around Nvidia faded. The Nasdaq Composite slid 1.48% to 23,734 and the S&P 500 lost 0.50% to 7,201, while the Dow Jones gain of 0.85% reflected rotation into industrial stocks. Tech sentiment was further weakened as Anthropic broke below its $83 IPO price.
global.europe: European markets closed lower on Tuesday following broader risk-off sentiment in global tech and industrial names. The DAX fell 1.26% to 25,018, while the Euro Stoxx 50 lost 1.16% to 6,004. Labour friction in Germany intensified as Volkswagen proposed a two-year pay freeze for 120,000 workers ahead of potential January strikes.
global.asia: Asian trading is experiencing severe technology-driven losses this morning. South Korea's KOSPI dropped 5.30% and Taiwan's TAIEX plunged 7.21% amid a heavy semiconductor sell-off. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 3.26%, led by a 14% drop in SoftBank, though Hong Kong's Hang Seng bucked the trend to rise 1.02%.

india: Indian benchmark indices suffered steep declines on Monday, with Nifty falling 1.75% to 25,350 and Bank Nifty tumbling 3.17% to 62,585 amid heavy profit-booking in financial and metal stocks. Markets were closed on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti. For today, GIFT Nifty indicates a gap-up opening, with technical analysts watching 25,700 as immediate resistance for Nifty.
commodities: Commodities saw sharp pullbacks overnight, with Brent crude dipping 1.86% to $87.71 per barrel while WTI rose 0.94% to $80.92. Bullion saw a steep sell-off as gold fell 2.43% to $3,562.70 and silver dropped 4.65% to $41.14. Lower industrial metal prices, including copper down 2.50% to $5.49, offer input margin relief for Indian capital goods and auto makers, while USD/INR remains steady at 92.90.

deep.title: Asian Semiconductor Rout Triggers Broad Risk-Off Across Regional Markets
deep.what: Asian equity bourses are seeing severe technology sell-offs this morning, led by South Korea's KOSPI dropping 5.30% and Taiwan's TAIEX falling 7.21%. Japan's SoftBank slumped 14%, dragging the Nikkei down 3.26%, while chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung fell over 7%.
deep.why: The pull-back follows a 9% overnight slide in Nvidia that unwound much of its Monday gains. Re-emerging doubts about return on investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure, combined with rising foreign portfolio flows rebalancing out of chip-heavy Asian indices, are triggering broad regional volatility.
deep.watch: Watch US inflation data released later today and the opening of US chip stocks tonight for signs of stabilization across global technology supply chains.

deep.title: APL Apollo and Tata Steel Face Investor Pushback on ₹28,000 Crore Deal Structure
deep.what: Shareholders and proxy advisory firms have raised concerns over the complex structuring of the ₹28,000 crore transaction between APL Apollo and Tata Steel. Under the proposal, APL Apollo will purchase two assets from Tata Steel for ₹28,000 crore funded by debt, while Tata Steel pays ₹15,510 crore for a 26.38% stake.
deep.why: Investors are troubled by valuation metrics and added debt burdens, alongside a expected 3 to 3.5-year wait for earnings accretion. Shares of both companies slid following the announcement as market participants weigh long-term downstream capacity gains against immediate balance sheet leverage.
deep.watch: Monitor proxy firm voting recommendations and upcoming shareholder Extraordinary General Meetings for potential deal term revisions.

deep.title: RBI Highlights Shift in Institutional Funds from G-Secs to Equities
deep.what: Reserve Bank of India Deputy Governor Rohit Jain noted that demand for long-term government securities has softened as pension funds and insurance companies redirect more capital toward equity markets. Separately, the RBI urged primary dealers to bid responsibly in debt underwriting auctions.
deep.why: Domestic institutional investors approaching their internal regulatory equity exposure caps are altering duration demand in the sovereign debt market. This shift has elevated yield volatility in long-dated paper and pushed primary dealers to absorb higher pricing risks during government bond auctions.
deep.watch: Watch upcoming G-Sec auction bidding details and sovereign yield curve spreads for signs of primary dealer margin pressure.

deep.title: Sanofi Agrees to Acquire Insmed for $41 Billion in Pharma Megadeal
deep.what: French pharmaceutical giant Sanofi has agreed to acquire US biopharmaceutical firm Insmed for $41 billion. Shares of Insmed surged 14% following the announcement, making it the largest healthcare M&A transaction in three years.
deep.why: Sanofi is acting to bridge potential revenue shortfalls scheduled for the end of the decade, when several of its core blockbusters lose patent protection. The heavy valuation reflects growing urgency among European pharma majors to acquire late-stage clinical pipelines despite high transaction premiums.
deep.watch: Track regulatory approval filings across US and European antitrust agencies expected over the coming months.

deep.why: If executed, the transaction would create the world's largest combined automotive, aerospace, and satellite technology conglomerate. However, governance experts flag significant valuation complexities, cross-holding conflicts, and potential shareholder litigation.
